question: How resilient are NASA's GES DISC and the Precipitation Processing System (PPS) as homes for data (integrity, recovery, copies, storage and access, track record), tagged against RRS-1, RRS-2, RRS-3, RRS-5, D-2 and D-3?
tier_reason: deep: dispute (proposed NASA science cuts and restructuring, Goddard consolidation) and high stakes for scoring two repositories

subquestions.question: Integrity (RRS-2): fixity/checksum checks by ESDIS, GES DISC and PPS (algorithm, frequency); CoreTrustSeal, ISO 16363 or WDS status; what NASA's data policy requires; whether Earthdata Cloud verifies stored copies.
subquestions.remaining_gap: No checksum algorithm or re-verification frequency is published for GES DISC, PPS or Earthdata Cloud; the Preservation Content Specification PDF and Cumulus ingest checksum documentation were not read; ISO 16363 not searched.

subquestions.question: Recovery (RRS-3): continuity or disaster recovery plans and tests; IG-26-005 and GAO-26-108556 findings on data systems; PPS near-real-time backup site.
subquestions.remaining_gap: No DR/COOP plan or test record found for ESDIS, GES DISC or PPS; the GAO-26-108556 full report was searched (files.gao.gov HTML) for data-system terms, not read line by line.

subquestions.question: Copies (RRS-1): any copy besides Earthdata Cloud (AWS us-west-2) or in a second region; what PPS keeps and for how long; whether the two are checked against each other.
subquestions.remaining_gap: Whether GES DISC deploys ORCA (Glacier/Deep Archive backup) is not published; PPS's long-term (arthurhou) archive retention and any GES DISC-PPS cross-check not found.

subquestions.question: Storage and access (D-2, D-3): storage design, the contracts and staff that run it (EED-3, ESDIS Next), dependence on Earthdata Login.
subquestions.remaining_gap: ENX award status after January 2026 not found; PPS's contractor and storage hardware not found; Earthdata Login funding not found.

subquestions.question: Track record (RRS-5): the 2025 shutdown, the 2026 cloud migration, the October 28-30, 2026 ingest pause, PPS's January 20, 2026 outage, and any data loss.
subquestions.remaining_gap: No after-action notices for the January 20, 2026 PPS shutdown or the October 2026 ingest pause; no statement either way on data loss; only page 1 (Aug 24-Nov 10, 2026) of GES DISC's 414 alerts was read.

claims.text: GES DISC (and so IMERG and GPCP V3.x) is held in one AWS Region: ESDIS treats multi-AZ storage within a Region as its off-site copy and uses S3 versioning and object lock instead of separate copies; GES DISC's on-premises archive became a rolling pass-through by September 30, 2026; the CMR record lists one S3 location; Cumulus's backup tool ORCA is documented as a Glacier/Deep Archive bucket created in us-west-2. No second-region, other-vendor or tape copy was found. Contradicts RRS-1; supports D-2 (single region).

claims.text: Follow-up: IMERG has two holders in different places. GES DISC stopped distributing IMERG V06 in July 2024 and said V06 'will continue to be available from' PPS's arthurhou archive at Goddard; during PPS's 2025 arthurhou outage, PPS pointed users to GES DISC for IMERG V07B. So for IMERG V07, PPS (Goddard, Maryland) and GES DISC (AWS us-west-2) hold copies, and for V06 PPS is the only holder named. No cross-check between the two is published. For IMERG this partly supports RRS-1 (two separate sites) but not its 'verified' part.

This argues against routine content checks catching such faults (RRS-2) and is a repaired defect, not a loss (RRS-5).

claims.text: Follow-up: ESDIS's EOSDIS-wide DAAC requirements (ADURD, 423-10-69 Rev B, effective March 2017, listed expiration March 2022) require that each DAAC's system 'ensure data integrity through the use of checksums' at ingest, archive and distribution, 'in order to satisfy interface requirements with external systems'. No re-verification interval is stated. NASA's Preservation Content Specification (Rev C, 2022) treats fixity information as 'implementation details'. So checksums are required for transfers, but RRS-2's quarterly-or-better re-check is not required by any published NASA document.

claims.text: Follow-up: the same ADURD requires each DAAC to keep 'an off-site backup copy of all other data that would be impossible or difficult to recover', listing products only as 'selected data products, depending on need', and allows the backup to sit 'in a NASA Cloud archive'; it also requires 'the capability to restore its archive'. A second copy of all products such as IMERG or GPCP is therefore not required, and no test of the restore capability is published. Neither supports RRS-1 nor RRS-3 for GES DISC.
